# ARK Identity Server

> Self-hosted OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect identity provider for ASP.NET Core (NuGet Ark.oAuth.Oidc), with client libraries for .NET (NuGet Ark.oAuth.Client), Python (PyPI ark-oauth-client), Node (npm ark-oauth-client-node) and the browser (npm ark-oauth-client-js, for single-page apps). The clients are ports of each other and share one version number. Multi-tenant at the protocol layer; administered by one operator tenant. Runs on SQLite, MySQL or PostgreSQL. MIT. Repository: https://github.com/ir-dev/ark-oauth-oidc

Source of truth is the code. Where a document and the source disagree, follow the source and say so.

## Integrate a client: the whole of it

Only two settings are required: `authority` (the issuer, `{BaseUrl}/{TenantId}`, tenant segment included) and `client_id`. Endpoints, signing keys and capabilities come from `{authority}/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Never hard-code endpoints or paste a public key.

- .NET: `builder.Services.AddArkOidcClient(builder.Configuration);` (section `ark_oauth_client`), then `app.UseRouting(); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization();` in that order. Root namespace `Ark.oAuth`.
- Python: `auth = add_ark_oidc_client(app, {"authority": A, "client_id": C})`; protect with `@auth.require_claims("x")`; user via `current_ark.user`.
- Node: `const auth = arkExpress({ authority, clientId, redirectUri, secret }); app.use(auth); app.get('/x', auth.requireClaims('x'), h)`.
- Browser / SPA: `const ark = new ArkBrowserClient({ authority, clientId }); await ark.init();` then `ark.signinRedirect()`, `ark.signoutRedirect()`, `ark.fetch(url)`. A public client: register it with auth method `none` (PKCE, no secret) and add the app's exact origin to the provider's `ark_oauth_server:Oidc:CorsOrigins`, or every token request fails as `Failed to fetch`. `ark.fetch` sends the token only to the page's origin and `apiOrigins`. Adapters: `ark-oauth-client-js/react` (`<ArkProvider>`, `<RequireArk claims>`, `<ArkCallback>` on the `/signin-oidc` route), `/next`, `/vue`, `/angular`. `await ark.checkSetup()` reports CORS and discovery problems.
- APIs (bearer): .NET `AddArkOidcApi`, Python `add_ark_oidc_api`, Node `arkBearer`.

## Run the identity provider

- Zero-config (since 2.1.3): `builder.AddArkIdp();` then `app.UseArkIdp();`. Unconfigured, every page goes to the setup wizard at `/ark-idp/setup` (organization and logos, public URL and tenant, database with test, RSA key generate/import, administrator, users and SMTP, protocol options, review and install). The same process becomes the IdP with no restart. Remote access needs the setup code from the start-up log. Sample: `dotnet run --project Ark.oAuth.Oidc/Ark.oAuth.Oidc.QuickStart`.
- Configured (released): `AddArkOidcServer(builder.Environment)` + `AddArkOidcClient(builder.Configuration)`; pipeline `UseRouting -> UseArkOidcCors -> UseArkAuthData -> UseArkOidcClient -> UseAuthentication -> UseAuthorization`. Section `ark_oauth_server` (TenantId, BaseUrl, Provider sqlite|mysql|postgres) + `ConnectionStrings:ArkAuthConnection`. `AdminUser:Password` from user-secrets or env, never appsettings.

## Onboard an application

`POST /api/oauth/v1/provision/client` with `{ client_name, user_name, redirect_uris, post_logout_redirect_uris, claims?, client_logo? }` creates the client, registers redirect URIs, creates or reuses the user and writes the user-client access mapping. `409 client_exists` means nothing was written. `POST /api/oauth/v1/provision/user` maps another user to an existing client. UI: `/{tenant}/admin/provisioning`.

## Govern tenants and instances (operator only)

Caller: the operator's console session, or a `client_credentials` token issued to `{TenantId}_machine` with scope `client.register` (secret from a vault: `ark_oauth_server:Management:MachineClientSecret`). Base `/api/oauth/v1/`:

- `tenant/list`, `tenant/upsert` (each tenant: own issuer, signing key, JWKS, branding)
- `client/list|upsert|delete`, `client/secret/reset`; `user/list|upsert`; `user/client/claims/upsert|delete` (Ark claims per user per client)
- `activation/user`, `activation/client` (`is_active:false` revokes sessions and refresh tokens at once)
- `data/summary`, `data/export` (optional AES-256-GCM passphrase), `data/import/analyze` then `data/import/apply` (`mode` replace|merge_skip|merge_overwrite + `plan_hash`; replace needs `confirm` = operator tenant id), `data/reset` (`confirm` = operator tenant id)
- Schema upgrades apply themselves at start-up on every provider. Never edit database rows. Ask the human before a reset or a replace import.

## Agents: A2A and MCP (since 2.4.2)

- An agent or MCP server is an ordinary confidential client. The client being called lists its callers (`a2a_callers`: client_id, claims, delegate_users); an empty list, the default, means nobody.
- As itself: `client_credentials` + `audience` (or `resource`) = the target's client_id. For a user: token exchange (RFC 8693) with a token issued or addressed to the caller. The token's `aud` is the target's client_id, `act` is the chain, `ark_claims` are the user's own at the target. Lives 300 s at most, no refresh token.
- Libraries: .NET `ArkAgentTokens.GetTokenAsync` / `AddArkAgentApi` / `ArkActors`; Python `agent_token` / `verify_agent_token` / `agent_actors`; Node `agentToken` / `verifyAgentToken` / `agentActors`. Never forward a received token; exchange it.
- MCP server: register it with its URL as the `client_id`, so an unmodified MCP client's `resource=<url>` resolves. Publish in `scopes_supported` only a scope the calling clients hold (`profile`), and check `ark_claims` in the tools.
- The IdP is itself an MCP server (after 2.4.2, [MCP.md](https://github.com/ir-dev/ark-oauth-oidc/blob/main/Ark.oAuth.Oidc/Ark.oAuth.Oidc/MCP.md)): `/ark-idp/mcp` sets it up (bearer = setup code) and is the operator's level afterwards, `/{tenant}/mcp` administers a tenant, `/{tenant}/mcp/{client_id}` is one application. Request a token with `resource` = the endpoint; `mcp.read` looks, `mcp.manage` changes. Start with `setup_status`, `host_overview` or `tenant_overview`. `{endpoint}/server-card` and `{endpoint}/config` are public.
- Up to 2.4.2, and to keep the tool list your own, an agent that must manage the IdP goes through a gateway MCP server that alone holds the machine credential. A browser sign-in by a third-party MCP client is not bound to that third-party server: there `resource` is ignored on the authorization code flow.

## Rules that cost the most time

- Map the user to the client, or sign-in fails exactly like a wrong password.
- Register both redirect URIs byte for byte: `/signin-oidc` and `/signout-callback-oidc`.
- Scopes on a client are a whitelist; an unregistered scope is rejected. `offline_access` yields a refresh token.
- Authorize on `ark_claims`, not scopes. Read the access token per request; never cache it.
- Never add a route at the callback path. Sign out of the local session and the provider.
- Shared browsers: enable the account switch with required claims: .NET `AccountSwitch:RequireArkClaims` + `RequiredClaims`; Python `account_switch.require_ark_claims` + `required_claims`; Node and browser `accountSwitch.requireArkClaims` + `requiredClaims`.
- Never hand-roll OAuth; never recreate the v1 shape (pasted `rsaPublic`, custom callback route, no state/nonce).
- .NET: both packages target `net10.0` from 2.3.0 (`net9.0` up to 2.2.1); keep `Microsoft.IdentityModel.*` on one version (8.23.0 from 2.3.0). No implicit, hybrid, ROPC, plain PKCE or SQL Server.
- The repository is public: never write a secret into a tracked file. Do not commit or publish unless asked.
